title: LIVS: A Pluralistic Alignment Dataset for Inclusive Public Spaces

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating text-to-image generated public spaces using an 'Accessibility' criterion (checking for ramps, tactile indicators, etc.) and analyzing the preference ratings of annotators with self-reported mobility or mental disabilities.
Assessing image outputs against 'Diversity' and 'Inclusivity' criteria for demographic representation and comparing multi-criteria preference scores from ethnic minority participants.
Grouping and comparing human preference annotations of generated urban spaces across different age cohorts (e.g., elderly vs. adult) within an intersectional analysis.
Analyzing multi-criteria evaluations (such as safety and comfort) of text-to-image generated public spaces across different gender identities as part of an intersectional scoring framework.
Tracking and comparing multi-criteria preference scores from annotators who self-identify as LGBTQ+ against other intersectional demographic groups.
Evaluating images against the 'Inclusivity' criterion, specifically looking for the model's ability to generate cultural markers, support for cultural/religious needs, and multilingual signage.
